presets.label: Head-on, 20 km apart
presets.note: Same altitude, closing at 400 m/s. The modified tau falls to 35 s at 14.7 s, and the loss of well-clear lasts until the intruder leaves the DTHR circle behind ownship at 53.1 s.

presets.label: Crossing at 90 degrees
presets.note: Both aircraft at 200 m/s on perpendicular tracks, 30 m apart vertically.

presets.label: Random encounter, intruder descending
presets.note: From the realistic encounter set: the intruder descends at 5,300 fpm into the 450 ft band.

presets.label: Near miss outside DTHR
presets.note: The horizontal miss distance is slightly larger than DTHR, so there is no loss of well-clear at any time.

presets.label: Vertical-only approach
presets.note: Horizontally inside DTHR with no relative horizontal motion, descending into the 450 ft band.

presets.label: Buffered table, TCOA = 20 s
presets.note: Vertical closure at 20 m/s: the band widens to |vz| x TCOA = 400 m before the aircraft reach the same altitude (SEM-3).

presets.label: Exact tangency (HMD = DTHR)
presets.note: The semantic cliff: on an exactly tangent path the horizontal violation set is 35 s long (here from -15 s to 20 s, so the loss within the lookahead lasts 20 s), and on a path one ULP further out there is no loss at all. Both implementations resolve this case correctly.

presets.label: Tangency with TTHR = 0
presets.note: Non-cooperative table: the exact loss is a single instant, so there is no conflict (SEM-7). The original agrees; the regenerated version reports a conflict lasting 0.2 microseconds. The case is inside the boundary band.

presets.label: Boundary contact (SEM-8)
presets.note: Exactly on the DTHR circle and moving tangentially away: WCV(s, v) holds at t = 0, but under the DAIDALUS convention this is not a violation. All implementations follow the convention.

presets.label: No relative motion at DTHR
presets.note: Closed boundary (NUM-3): at exactly DTHR, the loss lasts for the whole lookahead.

presets.label: Level flight at exactly ZTHR
presets.note: A vertical separation of exactly 450 ft with vz = 0 is inside the vertical band at all times.

presets.label: Stationary snap (NUM-2)
presets.note: About 2 micrometers inside DTHR, drifting apart at 0.27 micrometers per second. DAIDALUS treats this as no relative motion and reports 180 s of loss, while the exact exit is at 6.9 s. The oracle found this case in run 1, and the behavior is kept as a convention that both implementations follow.

presets.label: Boundary band: near tangency, short loss
presets.note: Within 1e-9 of the HMD cliff, with a short exact loss. The original reports no conflict and the regenerated version reports a conflict, in agreement with the exact semantics.

presets.label: Boundary band: near tangency
presets.note: The horizontal miss distance exceeds DTHR by 4e-13 m (less than two ULPs of DTHR), so under the exact semantics there is no loss. The original reports 8.8 s of loss (the 35 s tangency interval, clipped by the vertical window); the regenerated version reports none.

requirements.title: Inputs and outputs
requirements.text: Inputs: ownship and intruder position/velocity (so, vo, si, vi) as 3-vectors in a local Euclidean frame (m, m/s); lookahead bounds B, T (s); thresholds DTHR, ZTHR (m), TTHR, TCOA (s). Outputs: detection interval [t_in, t_out] within [B, T], or the empty encoding (+inf, -inf); a conflict flag; a violation flag.

status.evidence: Same encoding of empty results ((+inf, -inf)) on all vectors

requirements.title: Threshold domain
requirements.text: DTHR, ZTHR > 0 and TTHR, TCOA >= 0. The code does not reject other values: every setter and the 4-argument constructor silently replace a threshold by its absolute value, and zero is accepted.

status.evidence: Original: negative and zero thresholds computed without complaint (6 of 6). Regenerated: rejected with BadThreshold (6 of 6)

requirements.title: Lookahead domain
requirements.text: Interval detection assumes 0 <= B < T. B almost equal to T is an instantaneous check evaluated on [B, B+1]; B > T returns no conflict.

status.evidence: Original conflictDetection: B > T yields an inverted 'conflict' [10, 50]; B < 0 yields a loss starting in the past. Regenerated: BadLookahead

requirements.title: Operating ranges and threshold tables
requirements.text: Horizontal speed 10-700 kt, vertical speed +/-6000 fpm, altitude 100-50,000 ft, lookahead 180 s. Threshold tables in use: DO-365 DWC Phase I (0.66 nmi / 450 ft / 35 s / 0 s), Phase I preventive (700 ft), Phase II (1500 ft / 450 ft / 0 s), non-cooperative (2200 ft / 450 ft / 0 s), buffered DWC and preventive (1.0 nmi / 450 or 750 ft / 35 s / TCOA 20 s).

status.evidence: All six DO-365 threshold tables, speeds to 700 kt, vertical rates to 6000 fpm, lookahead to 180 s

requirements.title: Finite inputs
requirements.text: Positions, velocities, thresholds and lookahead are assumed finite. Nothing in the component checks this; behavior on NaN or infinity is unspecified and is measured by the fuzz check.

status.evidence: Original: answered on all 54 non-finite inputs, 'no conflict' in 42 of them for an encounter that is a violation when uncorrupted. DAIDALUS's top-level API screens NaN aircraft states, not infinities. Regenerated: NonFiniteInput on all 54

requirements.title: Only relative state matters
requirements.text: All outputs depend only on s = so - si and v = vo - vi (translating both aircraft, or adding the same velocity to both, changes nothing).
requirements.pvs: WCV(s, v) is stated on relative vectors

status.evidence: 3,000 / 3,000 translated vectors give the same answer

requirements.title: Horizontal well-clear violation (modified tau)
requirements.text: |s_h|^2 <= D^2, or (HMD^2 <= D^2 and 0 <= taumod <= TTHR), where HMD^2 = |s_h + tcpa*v_h|^2, tcpa = -(s_h.v_h)/|v_h|^2 (0 if v_h = 0), and taumod = (D^2 - |s_h|^2)/(s_h.v_h) if s_h.v_h < 0, else -1.

status.evidence: 55,795 / 55,795 decisions outside the band match exact semantics

requirements.title: Vertical well-clear violation
requirements.text: |sz| <= ZTHR, or 0 <= tcoa <= TCOA where tcoa = -sz/vz if sz*vz < 0, else -1.

status.evidence: 55,795 / 55,795 decisions outside the band match exact semantics

requirements.title: Well-clear violation is horizontal and vertical violation
requirements.text: WCV(s, v) holds if and only if the horizontal (SEM-2) and vertical (SEM-3) conditions both hold.

status.evidence: 55,795 / 55,795 decisions outside the band match exact semantics

requirements.title: Detection interval is exact
requirements.text: For 0 <= B < T and every t in [B, T]: WCV(s + t*v, v) holds if and only if t_in <= t <= t_out. The endpoints are themselves violation times (closed interval).
requirements.pvs: WCV_taumod.WCV_taumod_interval_correct (proved in PVS for real arithmetic)

status.evidence: 8,655 intervals: max endpoint error 8.0e-07 s (original), 3.7e-07 s (regenerated)

requirements.title: Symmetry
requirements.text: Exchanging ownship and intruder does not change any output.
code: (consequence of SEM-2/3: both are invariant under (s, v) -> (-s, -v))

status.evidence: 3,000 / 3,000 swapped vectors give the same answer

requirements.title: Conflict flag suppresses near-instantaneous loss
requirements.text: conflict <=> t_in < t_out and t_in, t_out are not almost-equal (within 16348 ULPs, or both within 1e-13 of zero). The PVS detection function reports a conflict even when the violation set is a single instant; the code deliberately does not.
requirements.pvs: differs from WCV.WCV_detection at single-instant contacts

status.evidence: 55,795 / 55,795 conflict flags outside the band

requirements.title: Violation flag is derived from detection on [0, 1]
requirements.text: violation <=> detection on [0, 1] reports a conflict whose t_in is almost 0. Consequence: a state that touches the well-clear boundary only at t = 0 (for example exactly at DTHR and moving away) is not a violation, although WCV(s, v) holds at that instant.
requirements.pvs: differs from WCV(s, v) on the boundary set

status.evidence: 55,795 violation flags outside the band; 6 / 6 boundary touches follow the convention

requirements.title: Level-flight snap
requirements.text: A relative vertical speed with |vz| < 1e-13 m/s is treated as exactly zero.

status.evidence: Level-flight snap cases match the convention-adjusted model

requirements.title: Stationary-geometry snap
requirements.text: If |v_h|^2 < 1e-13 m^2/s^2 and |s_h| <= DTHR at the start of the vertical window, relative horizontal motion is treated as zero and the horizontal condition holds for the whole window. Consequence: when |s_h| is within about sqrt(1e-13)*T (6e-5 m for T = 180 s) of DTHR and the aircraft drift apart, the reported exit time can be later than the exact one by up to the whole lookahead. Preserved as a convention for drop-in equivalence.
requirements.history: Refined after oracle run 1: the first version stated the snap but not its consequence; the exact oracle found 2 of 600 near-stationary vectors where DAIDALUS reported 180 s of violation against an exact exit at 6.9 s and 175 s.

status.evidence: Matches the refined requirement; 2 vectors in run 1 exposed the original wording as incomplete

requirements.title: Closed boundaries
requirements.text: Every threshold comparison is <=, so boundary points are inside the well-clear violation volume.

status.evidence: Closed-boundary edge cases (exact DTHR, exact ZTHR) inside the volume

requirements.title: Tangency tolerance in the circle-exit root
requirements.text: When the circle-exit discriminant is within 16348 ULPs of zero it is treated as zero (tangent) instead of producing NaN.

status.evidence: 29 / 29 exact-tangency vectors resolved as conflicts by both

requirements.title: Semantic cliffs are a declared boundary band
requirements.text: The conflict decision is discontinuous at HMD = DTHR (the horizontal interval jumps from length TTHR to empty), at |s_h| = DTHR with zero relative horizontal velocity, and at |sz| = ZTHR in level flight. Inputs within relative margin 1e-9 of a cliff, or whose exact violation set is shorter than 1e-6 s (or misses by less than 1e-6 s), or that sit on a 1e-13 snap threshold (NUM-1/NUM-2), are boundary-band: any answer is accepted but recorded. Outside the band, answers are graded against the exact semantics with the NUM-1/NUM-2 conventions applied.
code: (derived by analysis of SEM-2/3; not stated in code or PVS)
requirements.history: Refined after oracle run 1: grading now applies the NUM-1/NUM-2 conventions, and the pure exact semantics is kept alongside so the convention gap is reported rather than hidden.

status.evidence: 3,125 boundary-band vectors: original agrees with exact in 3,056, regenerated in 3,085

requirements.title: Accuracy outside the band
requirements.text: Outside the boundary band, conflict and violation decisions equal the exact semantics (SEM-2..8) and interval endpoints are within 1e-6 s of the exact endpoints.

status.evidence: Max endpoint error 8.0e-07 s vs 3.7e-07 s (limit 1e-6 s)

requirements.title: Constant time
requirements.text: Closed-form evaluation: no loops or iteration; cost per call is independent of the inputs.

status.evidence: Closed form, no loops, in both

requirements.title: Throughput no worse than the original
requirements.text: Single-thread calls per second on the same vectors must be at least the original's.

status.evidence: See performance section

requirements.title: Explicit errors instead of silent answers
requirements.text: Reject non-finite inputs, out-of-domain thresholds and malformed lookahead with an explicit error (the original sanitizes or silently computes; see ENV-1, ENV-4).

status.evidence: 63 / 63 invalid inputs rejected with a typed error

requirements.title: Memory-safe, panic-free
requirements.text: No unsafe code; no panic for any input bit pattern.

status.evidence: 20,000,000 fuzz iterations: 0 panics, 0 malformed results; component crate forbids unsafe code

requirements.title: No heap allocation per call
requirements.text: The hot path allocates nothing (the original allocates vector and interval objects on every call).

status.evidence: 0 bytes per call vs about 210 bytes per call in the original
